title: Tech Note: Recording Information sent Between 4D Client and 4D Server
author: Jean-Yves Fock-Hoon, QA Manager, 4D, Inc.
featured_technology: SET DATABASE PARAMETER (ID 28, 4D Server Log Recording)
Named selections for large listbox display

historical_commentary.text: This note introduces 4D Server's request log recording feature (SET DATABASE PARAMETER ID 28), explains the raw log file's columns (time, PID, UID, CID, request ID, bytes in/out, duration), and provides a demonstration database that imports these text logs into a table and visualizes them via listboxes, Quick-Report-driven statistics, and 4D Chart graphs. It is foundational, companion material to TN 06-04's deeper analysis and captures a Client/Server-era performance-monitoring workflow built entirely from first-generation 4D tools (Quick Report, 4D Chart, named selections) rather than any built-in profiler. The core need to monitor and analyze client/server network traffic remains relevant to 4D Client/Server deployments today, though the specific visualization tooling (4D Chart, Quick-Report-to-XML) is dated relative to more modern 4D reporting and monitoring options.
related_updates: 4D Server's request logging mechanism and the general practice of analyzing client/server request traffic for performance tuning remain applicable in modern 4D Client/Server deployments

The specific visualization stack shown (4D Chart, Quick Report XML export) reflects mid-2000s 4D tooling that has since been supplemented by more modern reporting and monitoring capabilities in later 4D versions
